findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer declares the standard buffers adequate at pH 3.2 ("standard buffers are fine at pH 3.2") violating the must-not item and it misses the 1.68-buffer requirement the bracketing failure at pH 3.2 the 10 °C buffer-temperature condition and the 0.05 pH-unit check. Unmet: States the usual 4/7/10 buffer set is not sufficient for acidic water and a pH 1.68 (or 2) buffer is needed when acidic waters are measured; States the sample pH must fall inside the calibrated range so a 4/7/10 set does not bracket pH 3.2; States the calibration buffers must be within about 10 C of the sample temperature; States that a check of the buffer nearest the sample pH should be within about 0.05 pH unit of its value at that temperature or the system is recalibrated

scored 0 — The answer makes the minimum-frequency midday-drift and continuous-sonde points but omits the sampling-location exemption the DO post-calibration check details and the QA-plan drift-criteria condition and it violates a must-not by asserting the EPA SOP 'sets a different cadence than the USGS guidance' without any support for the USGS cadence. Unmet: EPA cadence includes an end-of-day calibration check except when the instrument is calibrated at each sampling location; DO post-calibration check is done in measurement mode recording DO temperature and barometric pressure for comparison against an oxygen-solubility chart; The SOP's own drift criteria apply only when the project quality assurance plan does not specify its own
